proposal.title: Synthesis of Experimental Autocatalytic Memory Foundations
proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on autocatalytic reaction networks (CRNs), specifically isolating the stoichiometric conditions required for irreducible autocatalytic cores. By distinguishing these cores—which function as non-equilibrium memory units—from simple transient responses, we clarify the boundary between persistent chemical states and heritable information. Evidence from bipartite König representation analysis provides the algorithmic basis for identifying these cores in metabolic networks. Future research focuses on evaluating the thermodynamic cost of this information storage.

proposal.title: Autocatalytic Memory and Chemical Network Dynamics
proposal.summary: Continued investigation into autocatalytic reaction networks as substrates for history-dependent memory. Evidence indicates that algebraic conditions on stoichiometric matrices, particularly in irreducible autocatalytic sub-networks, provide a structural foundation for bistability. Current research differentiates this history-dependent state from simple hysteresis by examining whether network dynamics enable the encoding and conditioning of complex distributions. Further experimental verification is required to bridge theoretical stoichiometric sub-network analysis with wet-lab measurements of state persistence under fluctuating environments.
